summary: Peer closing-training session between two closers. Michael Brideau asks Richard Claessen to role-play objections so he can practise isolating the true objection after the $6,000 price drop. They run a money objection, an 'I need to think about it' objection, and Richard teaches his 'ABC of fear' framework (Admit, Befriend, Convert) plus the airplane/skydive analogy and a 1-10 goal-importance scale. Michael openly states he is relearning the script and does not yet have talk tracks for spouse, fear or payment-plan logistics. Opens with roughly two minutes of unstructured debrief about recent lost deals before the roleplay starts.
notable: Michael reports a sharp drop in personal close rate: 'I don't think I've ever closed under 30%. And now I'm like, bro, it's been like six deals. only got one.'
Michael discloses acute personal financial pressure while actively closing: 'I am so tight financially... I got to close for , like, tomorrow kind of thing' and confirms he has no savings.
Both reps make ethnicity-based generalisations about prospects' willingness/ability to pay.
Richard references a $500 deposit being attempted by a prospect, indicating deposit-taking is in live practice.
Richard describes a prospect who 'was expecting three grand it was six grand' and walked despite affording it — a repeat price-expectation gap set upstream of the closer.
Michael says he is being coached by a 20-year-old ('now you're being coached by a 20-year-old'), indicating Richard Claessen's approximate age and seniority structure.
